key_insight: ST2M uses crystallographic symmetry to generate crystal candidates, achieving 96.37% structural validity while improving the joint rate of stability, uniqueness, and novelty.
engineering_relevance: Generating candidates under prescribed crystallographic constraints could streamline computational materials screening and discovery.
method: Represent crystals as sequences of independent occupied Wyckoff orbits.
Use Wyckoff-pattern conditioning and degree-of-freedom masks to constrain generation.
Jointly denoise discrete and continuous variables with a twin-branch Transformer.
evidence_signal: For known dataset patterns, 23.86% of generated structures met stability, uniqueness, and novelty criteria—a 68.15% relative improvement over the best baseline; first-principles calculations identified 21 previously unreported stable structures among selected low-predicted-energy candidates.
watch_item: First-principles validation covered selected candidates, so it does not establish the stability rate across all generated structures.
paper_title: Site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer for symmetry-constrained crystal generation
